reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E with its Borel measurable structure, every joint probability P on E times R whose actual first-coordinate pushforward P.map Prod.fst equals stdGaussian(E), every real polynomial p, and a supplied witness MemLp(z->z.2,2,P) for the actual response coordinate, make the following definitions. Let S={w:E | norm_E(w)=1} with its inherited topology and measurable structure, and denote the ambient representative of w:S by w_bar. For every mu:Measure S and x:E define predictor(mu,x)=integral_S p.eval(inner_product_E(w_bar,x)) dmu(w). Define V(mu,w)=2*integral_{E times R}(predictor(mu,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product_E(w,z.1)) dP(z), for every ambient w:E. Define grad(mu,w)=gradient(V(mu,.),w), the actual Mathlib full ambient gradient, and G(mu,w)=grad(mu,w)-inner_product_E(grad(mu,w),w) times w. Define c(w,u)=Real.arccos(inner_product_E(w_bar,u_bar)) on S times S. Define Q(mu,nu) as the infimum in the nonnegative extended reals of integral_lower_{S times S} ofReal(c(w,u)^2) dgamma(w,u), over actual measures gamma whose first marginal is mu and second marginal is nu. The empty feasible infimum is infinity; no optimizer is selected or asserted. All predictor and potential integrals are actual real Bochner integrals, totalized to zero if their integrands fail to be integrable. The gradient definition is totalized at points without the corresponding Frechet derivative. Then the following full conclusion holds: There exist C1,C2:R with C1>0 and C2>0, uniform for all subsequent laws and unit weights. For every probability mu on S, and every ambient w:E, the scalar function z->(predictor(mu,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product_E(w,z.1)) is genuinely Bochner integrable under P, and HasGradientAt(V(mu,.),grad(mu,w),w) holds. For every such probability mu and every w:S, inner_product_E(w_bar,G(mu,w_bar))=0 and norm_E(G(mu,w_bar))<=C1. For every probability pair mu,nu on S, Q(mu,nu)!=infinity and, for all w,u:S, norm_E(G(mu,w_bar)-G(nu,u_bar))<=C2*((Q(mu,nu)^(1/2)).toReal+c(w,u)). The response membership supplies almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm under the true joint law; no independence or product decomposition follows from the Gaussian marginal identity. All response values in V are the actual z.2. The constants are existentially chosen once, before every measure and unit-point quantifier, and may depend on the fixed E,P,p and its response moment data but not on mu,nu,w,u. The explicit integrability conclusion concerns the displayed cross term under P for every ambient w, not merely for unit or supported weights. The gradient assertion is a genuine full ambient Frechet differentiability conclusion, with derivative v->inner_product_E(grad(mu,w),v); it is not merely the use of a totalized gradient symbol. Mu is fixed when taking this derivative. The statement does not supply a further closed formula for grad involving a derivative polynomial or an adjoint operator. For a unit ambient point w, the definition of G is the orthogonal projection of the full ambient gradient onto w-perpendicular; for nonunit w it is only the stated algebraic subtraction. The norm and law-plus-angle comparison are asserted only at exact unit points of S and concern G, not an unrestricted bound on grad. The parameter probabilities may be arbitrary, including nonatomic laws. Definitions exist for arbitrary measures, while the analytic and transport-finiteness claims have the displayed probability premises. Finiteness of Q makes its extended square root finite and toReal its ordinary nonnegative real value, rather than its convention zero at infinity. Q=0 is allowed. No new metric or geodesic structure, chosen optimal coupling, differentiability in the law variable, positive-dimensionality assumption, or nonzero-polynomial assumption is asserted. If S is empty, the probability-conditioned clauses are vacuous but positive C1,C2 are still required to exist.

Predictor integrals use the parameter measure on S, potential integrals use P on E times R, and transport lower integrals use coupling measures on S times S.
quantifiers: For every E and its structures, joint probability P with its actual Gaussian first-marginal equality, polynomial p, and supplied response L2 witness, let S,predictor,V,grad,G,c,Q be fixed by their formulas. There exist strictly positive C1,C2:R before all subsequent universal quantifiers. The first block quantifies every mu:Measure S with probability; for every ambient w:E it concludes cross-term integrability and genuine HasGradientAt, and for every w:S it concludes orthogonality and the C1 norm bound. The second block quantifies every pair mu,nu:Measure S with both probability; it concludes Q(mu,nu)!=infinity and then the single C2 estimate for every w,u:S. No per-law or per-point choice of constants occurs.

There is no product-law assumption, independence, explicit feature derivative input, supplied norm constant, finite-support restriction, or cost-finiteness premise.

They may depend on the fixed E,P,p and the response moment information already contained in the fixed data; no formula, optimality, or dimension/joint-law independence is specified. V has literal coefficient 2. G has exactly one copy of grad minus its normal component, without an additional outer factor. The cost is exactly c squared, with real exponent 1/2 on the extended transport value. The final estimate has one C2 multiplying the sum of the finite root transport value and c(w,u), without further normalization or a particle-count factor. No assumption that Q or G is strictly positive is imposed.
